root.label: Chronic Progressive Multisystem Neurological Syndrome with Cognitive Impairment and Vertical Gaze Palsy
supporting_facts: Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia for 6 months
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
excluded_candidates: Alzheimer's disease: less likely due to presence of vertical gaze palsy and pyramidal signs
Parkinson's disease: less likely due to presence of cognitive impairment and tongue atrophy
salient_findings: Decreased 11C-CFT binding in bilateral basal ganglia
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del)

static_evidence_items.content: Demographics: 48-year-old woman
Chief complaint: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Family history: relative with memory problems after age 80
Neurological examination: Cognitive impairment
Neurological examination: Vertical gaze palsy
Neurological examination: Tongue atrophy
Neurological examination: Pyramidal signs
11C-CFT PET imaging: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
11C-CFT PET imaging: Almost total loss in caudate nucleus
DAT binding measurements: Left caudate: 0.35 (normal 1.55-2.07)
DAT binding measurements: Right caudate: 0.36 (normal 1.55-2.07)
DAT binding measurements: Left anterior putamen: 0.43 (normal 1.91-2.53)
DAT binding measurements: Right anterior putamen: 0.53 (normal 1.91-2.53)
DAT binding measurements: Left posterior putamen: 0.64 (normal 1.58-2.01)
DAT binding measurements: Right posterior putamen: 0.81 (normal 1.58-2.01)
Image Title: 11C-CFT PET in Patient and Healthy Participant
Image Description: Decreased 11C-CFT binding in bilateral basal ganglia, with caudate most severely impaired
Needle EMG: Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles
Needle EMG: Unremarkable nerve conduction studies and EMG in other regions
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies: negative in serum and CSF
Genetic testing: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
